newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA JSE 1997 PROSPECTS SEEN BULLISH - ANALYST.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA JSE 1997 PROSPECTS SEEN BULLISH - ANALYST.

text.p: South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) will benefit from a continued bull trend on world markets, and is likely to move ahead later this year and into 1998, an Old Mutual Unit Trusts portfolio manager said on Thursday.
Alwyn van der Merwe said prospects for the share market looked bullish as the threat of a significant hike in U.S. interest rates was receding amid the absence of inflationary pressures.
"The South African stock market may also receive a boost from offshore buying with a more stable rand adding to the attractions of the JSE," van der Merwe said in a statement.
Leading monetary officials have recently said that the rand, which depreciated by 29 percent against the dollar in 1996, could look forward to a far more stable year in 1997.

Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals told Reuters on Wednesday he saw the rand depreciating by less than the inflation differentials, of some seven to eight percent, between South Africa and its major trading partners.
Van der Merwe said current share price levels, by global standards, offered reasonable value and a switch to a far more bullish sentiment on local stocks would be seen this year.
Local institutional demand for equities would remain strong and the weighting of equities in portfolios could well increase.
Van der Merwe said he expected banking shares to perform well this year, with these institutions benefiting from widening margins if an anticipated decline in interest rates occured.

"After the completion of the heavy infrastructural spending of the past few years, banks now have the capacity to cut costs. Even if sector rating remain the same, there is ample room for prices to move higher," he said.
